sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: The **Rajput Period** represents the medieval era in Indian history dominated by various **Rajput** clans who claimed Kshatriya status and established powerful kingdoms.
Roughly spanned from the **7th century** (post-Harsha era) to the **12th century CE** (until the establishment of the Delhi Sultanate).
Northern, Western, and Central **Rajputana** (modern-day Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, and parts of Uttar Pradesh).
Prominent dynasties including **Chauhans of Ajmer**, **Gahadavalas of Kannauj**, **Paramaras of Malwa**, **Chandellas of Bundelkhand**, and **Sisodias of Mewar**.

Marked by intense regionalism, architectural marvels (temples and forts), fierce martial traditions under leaders like **Prithviraj Chauhan** and **Rana Pratap**, and significant resistance against early Islamic invasions.
Feudal system (**Samanta system**), fierce clan loyalty, code of honor (*Chhatradharma*), monumental temple architecture (Khajuraho, Dilwara), and decentralization of political power.
Crucial for questions on medieval history, regional kingdoms of Uttar Pradesh (like **Kannauj**), decisive battles (**Battles of Tarain**), and architectural landmarks.
Lack of political unity, mutual rivalry among **Rajputs**, outdated military tactics compared to cavalry-based invaders, and absence of a centralized standing army.

items.title: 1. Origin Theories of **Rajputs**
items.content:
• **Agnikula Theory:** Origin from the sacrificial fire pit at Mount Abu (mentioned in **Chand Bardai**'s epic *Prithviraj Raso*).
• **Foreign Origin:** Supported by historians like **Col. James Tod** and **V.A. Smith**, linking them to Hunas, Scythians, or Kushanas.
• **Indigenous/Kshatriya Origin:** Supported by **G.H. Ojha** and **C.V. Vaidya**, arguing they are descendants of ancient Vedic Kshatriyas.
• **Mnemonic for Agnikula Clans:** **'P'**lease **C'**all **P'**izza **C'**heese (Paramaras, Chauhans, Pratiharas, Chalukyas).

items.title: 2. The **Chauhans of Ajmer and Delhi**
items.content:
• Founded by **Vasudeva Chauhan** in the 6th century in Sambhar (Sakambhari).
• **Vigraharaja IV (Visaladeva):** Extended the empire, captured Delhi, and authored the drama *Harikeli*. Built the Saraswati Temple in Ajmer (later converted into **Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra**).
• **Prithviraj III (Prithviraj Chauhan):** The most famous ruler, hero of **Prithviraj Raso**.
• Fought the historic **Battles of Tarain** against **Muhammad Ghori**.
• **Mnemonic for Chauhan Capitals:** **S'**mart **A'**dmins **D'**ominate **(S**ambhar, **A**jmer, **D**elhi).

items.title: 3. The **Mewar Dynasty & Rana Pratap**
items.content:
• Ruled by the **Sisodia** (earlier Guhila) clan from their capital at **Mewar** (Chittorgarh).
• **Mahana Kumbha:** Built the **Kirti Stambh** (Tower of Victory) at Chittorgarh and was an accomplished musician/scholar.
• **Maharana Sanga (Sangram Singh):** United various **Rajputana** clans against **Babur** in the **Battle of Khanwa** (1527).
• **Maharana Pratap:** Fought the legendary **Battle of Haldighati** (1576) against Mughal Emperor Akbar's forces led by Man Singh, relying on guerrilla warfare with his loyal horse **Chetak**.

items.title: 4. Regional Dynasties: **Chandellas & Paramaras**
items.content:
• **Chandellas of Bundelkhand:** Capital at **Khajuraho** and Mahoba. Famous for building the world-renowned **Khajuraho Group of Monuments** (e.g., Kandariya Mahadeva Temple) under rulers like **Dhanga** and **Yashovarman**.
• **Paramaras of Malwa:** Capital at **Dhara**. **Raja Bhoj** was the greatest ruler—a scholar, poet, engineer (built Bhojpur lake), and patron of arts.
• **Gahadavalas of Kannauj:** Ruled western UP, founded by **Chandradeva**; **Jayachandra** was a prominent ruler during the Ghorian invasions.

items.title: 5. Society, Culture, and Architecture
items.content:
• **Feudal Hierarchy:** The **Samanta system** weakened central authority as regional lords held immense autonomy.
• **Position of Women:** Practices like **Jauhar** (mass self-immolation by women) and **Sati** emerged prominently during times of defeat to protect honor.
• **Temple Architecture:** Developed the **Nagara style**, characterized by curvilinear towers (*Shikhara*), pillared halls (*Mandapa*), and intricate carvings.
• **Literary Patronage:** Flourished with works in Sanskrit and Apabhramsha, including **Kalhana**'s *Rajatarangini* and **Jayadeva**'s *Gita Govinda*.

items.definition: Remember **'1191 Win, 1192 Loss'** for **Prithviraj Chauhan**. First battle he won against Ghori, second battle he lost due to lack of coalition support.
Use the acronym **PPCC**: **P**ratihara, **P**aramara, **C**hauhan, **C**halukya. These four clans claimed descent from the fire altar at Mount Abu.
Remember **'Kumbha -> Sanga -> Pratap'** (KSS). **Mahana Kumbha** (Builder/Kirti Stambh), **Maharana Sanga** (Fought Babur at Khanwa), **Maharana Pratap** (Fought Akbar at Haldighati).
Link **Khajuraho** to **Chandellas** using **'C for C'** (Chandellas built temples with Chaitya/Nagara style in Bundelkhand).
Remember **'Bhoj = Bhopal/Bhojpur & Malwa'**. Associated with scholarship, lakes, and the Paramara dynasty at Dhara.
The three famous **Chittor Jauhars** occurred under: 1) **Rani Padmini** (1303, Alauddin), 2) **Rani Karnavati** (1535, Bahadur Shah), 3) **Rani Phool Kunwar** (1567, Akbar).
Students often think **Prithviraj Chauhan** won both battles of Tarain. **Fact:** He won the **1st Battle (1191)** but lost the **2nd Battle (1192)** to Muhammad Ghori.

items.term: Mistake 2: Confusing Rana Sanga and Maharana Pratap
items.definition: Students mix up Mughal opponents. **Rana Sanga** fought **Babur** at Khanwa (1527), while **Maharana Pratap** fought **Akbar**'s general Man Singh at Haldighati (1576).
Many assume the Agnikula myth is historical fact. **Fact:** It is a legendary account popularized by **Chand Bardai** in *Prithviraj Raso*, not a proven historical origin.
Confusing Khajuraho location with Rajasthan. **Fact:** Khajuraho monuments are located in **Madhya Pradesh**, built by the **Chandella** dynasty of Bundelkhand.

items.term: Mistake 5: Creator of Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra
items.definition: Assuming Muslims built it from scratch. **Fact:** It was originally a Sanskrit college built by **Vigraharaja IV (Chauhan)** and later converted into a mosque.
Confusing Paramara capital with Delhi or Kannauj. **Fact:** The Paramaras ruled Malwa with their capital at **Dhara (Dhar)**.
The **Rajput Period** thrived from the **7th to 12th century CE** across Northern and Western India (**Rajputana**).
Characterized by numerous independent kingdoms, fierce regional rivalries, and the absence of a unified central political authority.
Key ruling families included **Chauhans** (Ajmer/Delhi), **Chandellas** (Bundelkhand), **Paramaras** (Malwa), **Solankis** (Gujarat), and **Gahadavalas** (Kannauj).
**1191 CE:** Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori. **1192 CE:** Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan, establishing Islamic political dominance.
Patronized **Nagara style** architecture, visible in the **Khajuraho temples**, **Dilwara Jain temples**, and various hill forts.
Dominated by the **Samanta (feudal) system**, rigid caste hierarchies, and the heroic codes of honor (*Chhatradharma*).
Saw the emergence of practices like **Jauhar** and **Sati** alongside traditional respect for women's honor in royal households.
Flourishing of Sanskrit literature, epics like **Prithviraj Raso**, and scientific/astronomical advancements under rulers like **Raja Bhoj**.
Unwavering resistance offered by Mewar rulers like **Maharana Sanga** and **Maharana Pratap** against external Turkic and Mughal expansion.
High-yield topics include **Tarain battles**, **Khajuraho builders**, **Rana Pratap**, and regional UP capitals like **Kannauj**.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, memorize the exact years of the Battles of Tarain (1191, 1192) and Khanwa (1527), as direct chronological questions are frequently asked.
Focus heavily on temple builders and their locations (e.g., Chandellas built Khajuraho, Solankis built Dilwara) for static GK matching questions.
Do not confuse Jayachandra of Kannauj with Prithviraj Chauhan; their rivalry is a major focal point in medieval Indian political history questions.
Be careful with the term 'Rajputana'—it refers to the geographical region of Rajasthan and parts of MP, not a single unified empire.

keyTakeaways: The Rajput Period bridged ancient India and the medieval Delhi Sultanate, marked by intense regionalism and clan rule.
Prithviraj Chauhan's defeat in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192) permanently changed the political map of Northern India.
The Chandella dynasty gave the world the architectural masterpiece of the Khajuraho temples in Bundelkhand.
Mewar represented the pinnacle of Rajput resistance, spearheaded by legends like Rana Sanga and Maharana Pratap.
Feudal decentralization (*Samanta system*) and mutual rivalries were the primary causes of the political downfall of Rajput kingdoms.
